Bimal Kumar Ray Chowdhury and others
Vs.
Sree Pachu Pramanik and others
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J:- This rule is directed against the order dated 22.4.2001 passed by the District Judge, Satkhira in Title Appeal No. 214 of 2000 rejecting the plaintiff petitioners application for staying the operation of the decree dated 24.9.2000 passed in Title Suit No. 48 of 1999 by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Satkhira. 

 2. The petitioners as appellants filed Title Appeal No. 214 of 2000 before the District Judge, Satkhira challenging the decree dated 24.9.2000 passed in Title Suit No. 48 of 1999, previously Title Suit No. 58 of 1991. 

 3. Mr. S. S. Halder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned District Judge clearly erred in law in rejecting the petitioner’s prayer for staying operation of the decree under challen illegally and arbitrarily and the same has occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Parimal Chandra Guha, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, opposes the rule and submits that the learned District Judge was fully justified in rejecting the petitioners, prayer for staying the operation the impugned judgment, which is not only not executable but also in which the petitioners were not parties at all. The learned Advocate further submits that Order 41 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not make any provision for staying operation of the decree under challenge and as such the petitioners 'prayer for staying the operation of decree under challenge in not maintainable in law. 

 5. We have gone through the provisions of Order 41 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, which provides for stay of proceedings by the appellate Court. From a careful reading of Order 41 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, we find no provision for staying operation of a decree under challenge. In only empowers the appellate Court on sufficient cause to stay the execution of a decree. In the instant case, there is no question of execution of any decree. The operation of a decree under challenge can be stayed by the appellate Court in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure under special circumstances, only for securing the ends of justice. No such exception has been made out by the petitioners in the present case. 

 6. In the facts of the case, we have no hesitation to find that the appellate Court rightly applied his judicial mind in the facts and circumstances of the case and rejected the prayer for staying operation of the decree under challenge on assigning good reasons. We do not find any illegality or legal infirmity in the impugned order occasioning failure of justice to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. We find no substance in the revision. 

 7. In the result, the rule is discharged and the impugned order dated 24.9.2001 passed by the learned District Judge, Satkhira in Title Appeal No. 214 of 2000 rejecting the petitioners prayer for staying the operation of the impugned decree is affirmed.
